newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ING silent on SBC Warburg/Dillon report.
newsitem.headline: ING silent on SBC Warburg/Dillon report.

text.p: Dutch financial services group ING Groep NV (ING) said on Thursday it had no comment on a report that Anglo-Swiss investment bank SBC Warburg would buy Dillon Read & Co.
The Wall Street Journal had reported SBC Warburg would buy Dillon Read, a U.S. investment bank in which ING owns a 25 percent stake, for $600 million, or three times book value.

ING announced on Wednesday it had broken off talks to buy the other 75 percent of Dillon Read from the firm's partners, adding it expected the partners to exercise their option expiring on June 30 to buy ING's 25 percent shareholding.
ING spokesman Wieger Sietsma said it was up to the Dillon Read partners to determine if they wanted to sell the firm, and to whom, once they exercised their option over ING's stake.
The Wall Street Journal also said the Dutch banking and insurance group had "tag along" rights to receive 25 percent of the total sale price.
But Siestma said: "We will not comment on the repurchase agreement with Dillon Read."
ING inherited the Dillon Read interest when it took over British merchant bank Barings in 1995.
